                                   Message

          With the passage of time Sarada Charan Dey College has stepped into 31st
year of its existence. This journey has not at all been very smooth; rather many odds
had to be overcome to achieve the present position. During this period, the college
has been able to get in touch with many learned faculty members and gather a lot
from their knowledge and experience. The college also get the opportunity to
achieve prosper and progress due to valuable inputs and advice from many
stakeholders and most importantly with the blessings of the God.
         The college is situated nearby National Highway-53 in a completely rural
ambience. In the midst of eye-catching scenic beauty with all round greenery and
scattered habitations, free from any hustle and bustle, the place is ideally suitable for
an educational institution with proper teaching-learning atmosphere. The college,
although began its journey with Arts stream and later Commerce stream has been
introduced along with Honours paper. Quality education is imparted through both
the streams under the able and tireless guidance of the experienced and
knowledgeable faculty members. A very cordial relationship is maintained between
the teachers and the students and every effort is made to ensure all round
development of the students, including their physical and mental development along
with educational aspects in order to make them self-reliant and confident.

         Being the Principal (i/c) of this College, I would like to convey my best
wishes to the new comers who are going to be part of this institution. In order to
provide the idea about the institution, College PROSPECTUS generally been
published yearly. I hope and expect that the student will get clear picture about the
college and able to maintain the glorious history of the institution under the ambit
of the NEP-2020.

                        ABOUT SARADA CHARAN DEY COLLEGE:

Sarada Charan Dey College, Kalinagaris a rural institution of higher education located in the
Hailakandi district of Assam and affiliated with Assam University. Established in 1992, the
college emerged from the collective vision and initiative of local social workers, academicians,
educationists, and public representatives who recognized the growing need for higher education
in the region.

The foundation of the college was laid following a general meeting held on 13 September 1992
at Annada Charan Girls High School. After detailed deliberations, the meeting unanimously
resolved to establish a degree college in the locality from the academic session of 1992. The
institution was named in honour of Late Sarada Charan Dey, a distinguished social worker and
patron of learning, to commemorate his enduring contribution to society and education.

The college began its academic journey in modest bamboo-structured classrooms constructed on
its own land through the dedicated efforts and support of the local community. Within a few
years, a reinforced cement concrete (R.C.C.) building was constructed with financial assistance
received from the local Member of the Legislative Assembly (M.L.A.), enabling the institution
to expand its academic and administrative activities.

In 1993, the college received permission to commence classes under Gauhati University.
Subsequently, following the establishment of Assam University in Silchar in 1994–95, the
college came under the affiliation of Assam University, Silchar. In recognition of its academic
standards and institutional development, the college was accredited by the National Assessment
and Accreditation Council (NAAC) in 2023. Further strengthening its academic standing, the
institution was granted permanent affiliation under Assam University, Silchar in 2026.

Since its inception, the college has consistently striven for academic excellence while promoting
the holistic development of students through active participation in games and sports, cultural
activities, and co-curricular programmes. The institution has made steady progress through the
collective efforts of its management, faculty members, students, and well-wishers.

A significant milestone in the developmental journey of the college was achieved in 2019, when
the institution received financial assistance amounting to Rs. 50 lakhs from the Government of
Assam for infrastructural development. With the construction of a new multi-storeyed academic
building, the administrative office of the college has been shifted to the newly constructed
premises. In alignment with the objectives of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, the
college is presently undertaking the development of digital classrooms and a digital library to
enhance the teaching-learning environment and modernize academic resources.

The institution also remembers with profound respect the invaluable contributions of Late Binoy
Krishna Dey, whose dedication, vision, and selfless service played a pivotal role in strengthening
 the foundation of the college and promoting the educational welfare of the locality. The college
gratefully acknowledges his noble efforts and pays heartfelt homage to his cherished memory.

Driven by its commitment to inclusive and quality higher education, Sarada Charan Dey College
continues to work towards academic advancement, infrastructural development, and the overall
empowerment of the rural student community.

                               VISION OF THE INSTITUTION


The college is guided by a clear and purposeful vision that reflects the educational and socio-
economic needs of the locality. The institution is committed to fostering an inclusive and learner-
centred academic environment that empowers students to achieve intellectual growth, social
responsibility, and personal excellence.

The specific vision of the college includes:

   1. To create a student-centred educational environment that enables learners to achieve
      academic excellence, develop diverse competencies, and attain their educational and
      career aspirations.
   2. To impart quality higher education to rural and economically disadvantaged students so
      as to equip them to face the challenges of modern life and emerge as responsible, self-
      reliant, and capable citizens of society.
   3. To expand access to educational opportunities in accordance with the needs of the
      community and to help students address socio-economic and cultural challenges through
      active participation in social development and nation-building activities.



                                         MISSION :

The College is guided by a mission to foster excellence in both curricular and co-curricular
activities while nurturing sound values, a spirit of unity in diversity, and leadership qualities
among students, enabling them to compete at the global level. Since a large number of students
in this locality belong to SC and OBC/MOBC communities, the College is committed to
uplifting these socially disadvantaged groups through inclusive educational initiatives and
support systems.
    Established with the aim of meeting the educational needs of economically vulnerable sections
   of society, the College strives to provide access to higher education for students who face
   financial hardships and social challenges. Special emphasis is placed on quality education and
   character building to ensure the holistic development of students and empower them to become
   responsible and capable citizens.

     Academic Programs offered by the college


Sarada Charan Dey College, Kalinagar is affiliated to Assam University, Silchar primarily offers the
Four-Year Under-Graduate Programme (FYUGP) in Arts and Commerce as per the National
Education Policy (NEP) 2020 as adopted by the University since 2023.

   Four-Year Under-Graduate Programme (FYUGP)
Under National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, the traditional three-year Bachelor’s degree has been
transformed into the Four-Year Under-Graduate Programme (FYUGP), characterized by multiple exit
points.

Like the traditional Bachelor’s degree, students are admitted to the FYUGP on having successfully
completed their higher secondary education. However, unlike the traditional three-year degree, in the
FYUGP, upon successful completion of two semesters (i.e. one year), a student has an option to exit the
programme with a certificate. Upon successful completion of four semesters (i.e. two years), a student
may exit the programme with a diploma. Upon successful completion of six semesters (i.e. three years), a
student may exit with a general three-year Bachelor’s degree.

 If and when a student continues to the fourth year with no arrears, she is eligible for the Bachelor’s
degree with Honours upon successful completion of the seventh and eighth semesters. A student stepping
into the fourth year with CGPA higher than 7.5 on averages may choose to get the more advanced
Honours with Research’ degree after completing a research-based dissertation.

 The credits earned by the students every semester are recorded in the Academic Bank of Credits (ABC)
so that even after exiting the programme with a certificate or diploma, a student may, in future, resume
further studies from where they left off.

  Course selection
Counseling on course selection will be done by teachers at the time of admission and at the
beginning of every semester.

 • Initially, a student has to select one Major (DSC) subject and two Minor (DSM) subjects from
among available options.

• Further, a student has to select from available options for SEC, IDC, AEC and VAC.

 • The choice of SEC is limited to the subjects which a student has already selected for her Major
(DSC) or Minors (DSM).

• The subject selected for SEC as well as IDC will remain the same in the subsequent semesters.
    Evaluation

   ❖ Evaluation of courses of 3 or 4 credits shall be out of 100 marks, and that for courses with 2
     credits shall be out of 50 marks.
         • For courses carrying 100 marks, the End-Semester Examination shall be of 70 marks,
              Internal Assessment (tests/assignments during the semester) shall carry 20 marks, and
              Attendance shall carry 10 marks.
         • However, for SEC, the End-Semester Examination shall be of 50 marks (Theory) and 30
              marks (Practical/Project/Field Work). Further, Internal Assessment shall carry 14 marks
              and attendance shall carry marks.
         • For AEC courses there shall not be any internal.

                                     ELIGIBILITY FOR ADMISSION

Students who have passed the Higher Secondary Examination (10+2) from any recognized Board or
Council, including the Assam Higher Secondary Education Council (AHSEC) or any other State Board,
and who wish to seek admission into FYUG courses under the NEP-2020 framework must fulfill the
stipulated norms as prescribed by Assam University, Silchar, the Directorate of Higher Education,
Assam, and the College authority.

                              GENERAL CONDITIONS

1. A student must register in Samarth-e Gov Portal.
2. A student must pass fromRecognized institution/ Board.
3. The admission depends upon seats availability (Intake Capacity) and reservationpolicy of the
Government (ST-7.5%, SC-15%, OBC/MOBC-27% and EWS-10%).
4. Any student who is physically disable will get special preference under PWD Category.
5. The character of the student must be good having no criminal record.
6. Admission based on Merit of the student governed by college Admission Committee.

                   STUDENTS SUPPORT AND PROGRESSION

     STUDENTS COUNCIL:

The Students’ Council of the College consists of elected student representatives and serves as a
representative body for all students. The election/selection of the Union is conducted every year as
per Government provisions. This Students’ Council is expected to cooperate with the College
authority for the all-round development of the institution.

 Electoral Literacy Club

The College has established the Electoral Literacy Club (ELC) to create awareness among
students in the age group of 18–21 years about their constitutional rights and duties. The club
also aims to familiarize students with the electoral process, including voter registration and
voting procedures.

As these students represent the future electorate and serve as pillars of Indian democracy, the
Electoral Literacy Club plays an important role in educating them about the significance of
voting rights and civic responsibilities.


 Grievance Redress Mechanism
The College has a Grievance Redressal and Anti-Ragging Committee to address any issues or
haphazard situations that may arise among students. A suggestion/complaint box has been
installed in the College where students can submit their grievances or complaints. The box is
opened in the presence of the Principal and faculty members for proper review and action. In
cases involving sensitive or critical issues, strict disciplinary measures are taken to resolve the
matter as promptly as possible. As the College is a rural-based institution, instances of
grievances are generally minimal.

In addition, the College has a dedicated Grievance Redress Cell. Students may contact the
Convenor of the Cell for any assistance or concerns. They are also encouraged to freely share
their views, suggestions, or complaints by using the suggestion/complaint box provided by the
Cell.

 Social-Cultural Cell

The College has an auditorium with a seating capacity of 500 people at a time. It serves as the
main venue for various cultural activities such as Social Week, Freshers’ Welcome Ceremony,
and Farewell Ceremony. The College also has a Cultural Cell that organizes different
programmes on red-letter days and other important occasions. In addition, the College promotes
  sports activities both within and outside the campus. Annual Sports are organized every
 academic year, and special prizes are awarded to the best sportspersons of the year.




   Library:
The college has a well-furnished library with a huge collection of books covering different courses.
The library facilities include reading room for students and teachers, newspapers, lending of books
and other materials. Question papers and other magazines booklet etc. are also available in the library.
By using library cards students can borrow books and other materials from library on all working
days from 10:00 am to 4 am for a period of 7 days.

   Computer Lab

There is a computer lab in the college to facilitate students, the basic courses of computer application
with a nominal cost.
  Incubation Centre:

The college has signed MOU with ITI, Badarpur Ghat where students can pursue many skill
development programs like electrician, beautician, tailoring, computer basic and diploma courses etc.,
on part time basis.
   Health care:

The college has first aid health care facilities and if required, the students be sent to Sarojini Primary
Hospital, college. Kalinagar which is adjacent to the college.

  Internal Compliance Cell:

 There is an ICC in the College to monitor sexual harassment and other women related issues (both for
students and staffs in the campus)

   Anti-Ragging Cell

 The College has a very active Anti-Ragging Cell functioning under the supervision of a
 designated faculty member. The cell plays a crucial role in ensuring a safe, disciplined, and harmonious
 campus environment. It remains constantly vigilant regarding any issues related to ragging and takes
 immediate preventive and corrective measures whenever necessary.In accordance with the strict
 directives of the University Grants Commission (UGC), the College constitutes the Anti-Ragging
 Committee every year under the Chairmanship of the Principal along with senior faculty members. This
 committee is responsible for monitoring student behavior, creating awareness about the ill effects of
 ragging, and ensuring strict compliance with anti-ragging regulations.

 The College adopts a zero-tolerance policy towards ragging, and any student found guilty of such
 misconduct is subjected to strict disciplinary action as per rules. Through regular awareness programmes,
 counselling and monitoring, the College ensures that a safe and welcoming environment is maintained for
 all students
 .**For any grievance or complaints: Contact Smti Minakshi Dey, Assistant Professor
(9401133606)




 Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR)
 Club
Establishing a Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) Club at Sarada . Charan. Dey College, founded in
2026, is a timely and progressive step that reflects the institution’s commitment to safety,
awareness, and holistic student development from its very beginning.

The DRR club would allow students to actively engage in awareness programs, disaster
preparedness training, first aid practice, and community outreach activities. These initiatives
would strengthen leadership qualities, teamwork, and problem-solving skills among students
while also promoting a culture of safety within and beyond the campus. By supporting the
formation of a DRR Club, Sarada . Charan. Dey College,demonstrates its vision of being more
than just an academic institution—it becomes a center for responsible citizenship and community
resilience. This initiative would set a strong foundation for a safer, more aware, and socially
engaged campus culture from the very beginning of the college’s journey.


        CO-CURRICULAR AND EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES:

                                       Wall Magazine


Sarada Charan Dey College publishes its wall magazines titled “ANURANAN” by the
Department of Bengali and “CONTEMPORARY” by the Department of Political Science.
These wall magazines serve as creative platforms for students to express their thoughts, ideas,
and literary talents.Students are encouraged to contribute writings such as poems, short articles,
essays, short stories, and also showcase their artistic works. This initiative helps in nurturing
creativity, enhancing writing skills, and developing critical thinking abilities among students.

Through active participation in these wall magazines, students gain confidence in expressing
themselves and improve their academic as well as co-curricular skills, making it an important
part of the College’s literary and intellectual development activities.



                                   National Service Scheme


Mahatma Gandhi, the Father of the Nation, believed in the principle of “Manava Seva Madhava
Seva”, meaning “Service to man is service to God.” He recognized that the nation could not
progress in the desired direction unless students and youth—who are committed, sincere, and
dedicated—were motivated to work for the upliftment of society.
 In this context, the National Service Scheme (NSS) was launched in 1969 during the Birth
Centenary of Mahatma Gandhi. This programme is implemented by the Ministry of Youth




Affairs and Sports with the motto “Not Me But You”, aiming to develop the personality of
students through community service.




The NSS unit of the College was officially established in 2023. However, students of the College
have been actively engaged in various social activities since the establishment of the institution.
The NSS unit undertakes several important initiatives on social issues such as prevention of early
marriage of girl children, dropout reduction campaigns, and surveys related to the Arunodoi
scheme, among others.
                                               SPORTS: -


The College has a playground where students regularly practice and play cricket and football.
The College football team has participated in several inter-college tournaments and has
consistently shown commendable performance with great enthusiasm. Badminton is also played
within the campus by both boys and girls. During the Social Week of the College different soprts
events are generally organized to promote the all-round development of students through a range
of academic, cultural, and co-curricular activities.


                                                 Yoga

The College authority has appointed a qualified Yoga instructor to guide students and staff in
regular yoga practice. Under the supervision of the instructor, yoga sessions are conducted to
promote physical fitness, mental well-being, concentration, and overall personality development.

These sessions help students and staff to manage stress, improve focus in academic and
professional activities, and maintain a healthy and balanced lifestyle. The practice of yoga also
encourages discipline, self-awareness, and a positive attitude towards life. Through regular
participation, the College aims to foster holistic development and enhance both physical and
mental well-being of the entire College community.
                       Rules and regulation

  The College follows a set of rules and regulations to maintain discipline and create a conducive
  academic environment. All students are required to abide by the rules framed by the College
  authority from time to time. Any violation of these rules and regulations may lead to disciplinary
  action as decided by the authority.

  Class Schedule and Attendance: -

  a) Classes for all courses are generally held from 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. (Monday to Saturday),
  except on holidays.

  b) The class schedule for all courses is normally displayed on the Notice Board.

  c) Holidays and vacations are notified as per the University list of holidays and Government
  notifications.

  d) Students are required to attend classes in their respective subjects, each of 45 minutes
  duration.

  e) A minimum of 75% attendance in classes is compulsory for all regular students, failing which
  they will be debarred from appearing in the end-term University Examinations.

Instructions for the students

      ❖ Students must come to the College in full uniform. No addition or alteration in the
        prescribed dress code will be allowed.
      ❖ Students are required to maintain discipline and follow the rules and regulations of the
        College to ensure a conducive educational environment.
      ❖ All forms of ragging are strictly prohibited. If any student is found guilty of engaging in
        ragging or illegal activities within the College campus, disciplinary action will be taken
        against him/her by the authority.
      ❖ Spitting on walls, corridors, classrooms, and examination halls is strictly prohibited.
      ❖ The use of mobile phones inside classrooms and examination halls is strictly prohibited.
      ❖ Hair style should be neatly cut and well groomed.
